title: Venn diagram template
subject: Mathematics
unit: Spring 2: Revision cycle 2: Geometry, vectors, statistics, calculus
source: Seeded from mathematics/y11 lesson 88 (Venn diagram template (printable, in the pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 88: Sets, Venn diagrams and probability. To understand set notation and Venn diagrams, and use them to find probabilities

blocks.text: Draw the rectangle round both circles for the universal set ξ. Write each value or count in the right region: A only, A ∩ B, B only, and outside both.

questions.q: ξ = {1, ..., 10}, P = primes, E = even numbers. List P ∩ E and P'.
Using the Arabic and Business Venn: P(neither)?
Is {2, 4} a subset of the even numbers? Write it with the symbol.

In a group of 50, n(T) = 28 (tea), n(C) = 22 (coffee), n(T ∩ C) = 9. (a) Draw the Venn diagram [3] (b) n(T ∪ C)' [1] (c) P(coffee only) [2] (d) P(tea | coffee) [2] (e) ξ = {x : x is an integer, 1 ≤ x ≤ 20}, A = {x : x² < 30}: list A [2] (f) Shade (A ∪ B)' and A' ∩ B on two copies of a Venn diagram [2]
questions.a: (a) T only 19, both 9, C only 13, neither 9 (b) 9 (c) 13/50 (d) 9/22 (e) A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} (f) outside both circles; B without the overlap
questions.model: (a) 28 - 9 = 19, 22 - 9 = 13, 50 - 41 = 9. (b) outside both. (c) 13 of 50. (d) 9 of the 22 coffee drinkers. (e) 5² = 25 < 30 but 6² = 36. (f) shading as described.

questions.a: 10 pupils study both, so they are counted twice: 25 + 18 + 7 - 10 = 40.
